page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores clocked up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and modern instruction extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 944 GB NVMe SSD, while GPU hardware acceleration is absent.

Benchmark measurements reflect robust per-core processing and standard throughput characteristics across moderate concurrency. The AMD core architecture attains top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3793.39) as well as single-threaded data compression, reaching 41.18 GB/sec in gzip and 18.21 GB/sec in bzip3. Conversely, multi-threaded operations and aggregate throughput perform at average levels due to the restricted 4-vCPU ceiling, demonstrated by an average PassMark CPU score of 10054.5 and multi-core stress-ng performance of 7580.4. Uncached memory read bandwidth tests reach 48.62 GB/sec with 34.0 GB/sec write throughput, supporting a Redis SET performance of 7.7 million operations per second.

The constrained core configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications bound by per-core software licensing. Rather than provisioning a full 16-vCPU instance to access 128 GB of RAM, users attain high memory capacity alongside fast local NVMe storage on a reduced 4-vCPU profile. The primary tradeoff is bounded parallel throughput, making the instance less suited for heavily parallelized multi-core computing or large-scale AI inference.
This server type is suitable for memory-dense, cache-heavy workloads including in-memory relational databases, Redis caching layers, memory-bound data analytics, and intermediate ETL staging.
